cli.help.audit:
Usage: {command} audit [--json]

Measures the documentation against the maturity levels of the standard (1 Skeleton to 4 Takeover) and lists, in order, what to do to reach the next level. Writes {work}/audit.md and {work}/audit.json; exit code 0 whatever the level.

Options
  --json                   the full result on the standard output

DOC_KIT_NO_BROWSER=1: the table widths are not measured (no browser).
cli.help.bricks:
Usage: {command} bricks [<id|preset>] [--json]
       {command} bricks run [<id|preset>…] [--deps] [--stale] [--force] [--network] [--tools] [--json]

The bricks of the project (standard/bricks.json): each part that can be run again on its own — every facts source, the external tools, the documentation audit. With no argument, the state of every brick (up to date, out of date, never produced, on demand, disabled) and why; with an id, that brick: what it needs and how it runs; with a preset, its bricks and their states. `run` runs the bricks named, or every brick out of date with --stale, in the order of their needs; the facts are read in one run; a brick the project disables never runs. bricks.enabled and bricks.disabled in doc.config.mjs choose the bricks of the project (ids or presets: facts, full).

Options
  --deps                   also run what the bricks need, when it is not up to date
  --stale                  every brick missing or out of date (with names: only those of them that are)
  --force                  with --deps: run the needs even when they are up to date
  --network                lets inputs.repos fetch the shared repositories, and facts ask the public registries
  --tools                  lets the bricks that require the external tools run (facts.tools); skipped without it
cli.help.build:
Usage: {command} build [--draft] [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--output <file>] [--space <id>]

Builds the site: one self-contained HTML file. Strict by default: any problem fails (exit code 1) and nothing is written. When content/toc.json declares spaces, also one file per space, from which the other spaces are removed (spaces.export false: the full site alone).

Options
  --draft                  turns the problems into warnings (missing pages and captures are tolerated)
  --date YYYY-MM-DD        date shown in the site, for reproducible builds
  --output <file>          another file than the configured output (with --space: the file of that export)
  --space <id>             only the export of that space
cli.help.capture:
Usage: {command} capture [patterns…] [--plans <folder>] [--preview] [--no-session] [--yes] [--compare] [--stale] [--trace] [--verify]

Takes the screenshots of the capture plans in a headless browser: images/<id>.webp and images/zones/<id>.json. With a session the run is read-only: every request other than GET, HEAD and OPTIONS is blocked. Refused with capture.mode "none". With capture.target "production": always read-only, a banner "PRODUCTION — read-only · N screenshots · <url>" and a confirmation (default No).

Arguments and options
  patterns…                only the ids matching one of the patterns (* any characters, ? one)
  --plans <folder>         another plans folder, relative to the project
  --preview                also writes {work}/<id>.zones.png, the zones drawn in red
  --no-session             without the saved session (public pages)
  --yes, -y                confirms a production capture in advance (required without a terminal)
  --compare                only replaces an image that really changed; its zone file is always refreshed
  --stale                  only the captures listed in {work}/sync-report.json ({command} sync); implies --compare

--trace keeps the Playwright trace of each failed capture in {work}/traces/<id>.zip (network, DOM snapshots, screenshots, step by step), opened with npx playwright show-trace.

--verify replays the plans as tests: each page is opened, its actions played, its frame and zones located, read-only as always, but no image or zone file is written. A plan whose screen changed (a button renamed, a field gone) fails with the zone it could not find: run it in CI against the demo, or before a release.
cli.help.check:
Usage: {command} check [coverage|links|tables|images|secrets|all] [--width <px>] [--threshold <KB>]

Runs the checks, all of them by default (coverage is skipped when no adapter is configured).

Checks
  coverage                 every element inventoried by the coverage adapters is cited
  links                    internal links, anchors and journey steps
  tables                   tables wider than the reading column (opens every page)
  images                   orphan, missing, heavy and outdated images
  secrets                  .env values, GUIDs, keys and tokens in the site and its sources

Options
  --width <px>             window width of the tables check (default 1440)
  --threshold <KB>         weight above which an image is heavy (default 200)
cli.help.connect:
Usage: {command} connect [--url <url>] [--forget] [--as <role>]

Opens the application in a visible browser: you sign in yourself (SSO and MFA work), then press Enter. The session is saved in {work}/session.json, a secret ignored by git. Refused with capture.mode "none", except --forget. With capture.target "production", a production line comes first: sign in with your own account.

Options
  --url <url>              another address than app.url
  --forget                 deletes the saved session
  --as <role>              saves the session as {work}/session-<role>.json instead, for that role in probe (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.13)
cli.help.demo:
Usage: {command} demo

Runs the demo data script of the configuration (capture.setup) in its own Node process, before a capture run. Refused with capture.target "production": a demo data script never runs against production. No option.
cli.help.dev:
Usage: {command} dev [--port <n>]

Builds the site in draft mode, serves it on 127.0.0.1, opens the browser and rebuilds on every change: the page reloads by itself. Ctrl+C stops. With spaces, the export of each space is also served at /space/<id>.

Options
  --port <n>               port of the server (default: the first free port from 4400)

DOC_KIT_NO_OPEN=1: prints the address without opening a browser.
cli.help.doctor:
Usage: {command} doctor [--network]

Checks the environment (Node, kit, Chromium, skill) and the project (configuration, paths, version, application folder, capture target, .gitignore, session, contrasts; ⚠ production without any capture.forbidden route): one line per check, ✔ ⚠ ✖, each problem with its fix.

Options
  --network                also checks that the application answers at app.url
cli.help.export:
Usage: {command} export <target> [--with-dist] [--zip]

Writes a self-contained copy of the project into <target> (a new or empty folder), engine vendored: it rebuilds without the kit.

Options
  --with-dist              also copies the built site (dist/), and the exports per space wherever they are
  --zip                    also writes <target>.zip
cli.help.facts:
Usage: {command} facts [--source <name>]... [--network] [--tools] [--json]

Reads the application code (app.dir) and writes one file per source, facts/<source>.json (paths.facts), in the documentation project — never in the application: dependencies, stack (the stacks found, each language of the code and whether the kit reads it), env, api, screens (the screens of the front-end routers), db, infra (what the infrastructure files declare: resources, workloads, images, environments), behaviours (how a search, a filter, a sort, a page, a form behave: hints for the feature sheets), agents, secrets, security, quality, tests, modules, history. Used by ::facts{source="…"} and by the takeover page types (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.9, §6.13).

Options
  --source <name>          repeatable: only these sources (default: all of them)
  --network                dependencies: also checks that each direct package exists in its registry; quality: direct dependencies behind their latest version — only the name of a package a lock file proves public (package-lock.json, yarn.lock v1, poetry.lock, uv.lock), never one known only from a manifest, pnpm, yarn berry or a Pipfile.lock, nor one declared private (scope with its own registry, private index, workspace or local package); with --tools, osv-scanner may download its database (no name sent)
  --tools                  also runs gitleaks, osv-scanner (offline only), syft and knip when they are on the PATH (facts/tool-<name>.json: a status and an allowlist of fields, never a secret or a line of code), and semgrep when review.semgrep names a local rules folder; a missing tool is reported, never an error
cli.help.globals:
Global options: --project <dir>, --json, --verbose, --lang en|fr (message language), --profile, --help, --version
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 failed check · 2 usage or configuration · 3 environment
cli.help.init:
Usage: {command} init [app-dir] [options]

Creates the documentation project of an application in <app-dir>/docs/manual/. app-dir is the application root (default: the current folder); the front end may sit in a sub-folder. Detects the framework, the product name, the version and the .env files, and shows a recap before writing anything, also with --yes. Asks where the screenshots are taken: local or demo application, production read-only, or none. In a terminal, once the project is written: offers to open the browser to sign in (npm install, then connect) and a first test screenshot (capture --preview); never with --yes.

Options
  --dir <folder>           project folder, relative to the application (default docs/manual)
  --name "…"               product name (default: metadata.title of a Next.js layout, else package.json without its -frontend, -web… suffix, else the folder name)
  --lang en|fr             language of the site (asked without --yes) and of the messages
  --url <url>              application URL (default: the port of the dev script)
  --framework <name>       next, react-router or none: the coverage adapter (default: detected)
  --auth <adapter>         sign-in: manual (default), none, nextauth, api-me, local:<file>
  --capture app|none       app (default): screenshots of the application; none: no screenshot, each screen is described by a table
  --target <where>         local, demo or production (read-only: capture.readOnly true, a confirmation before each capture run; needs --url with --yes); default: local for a localhost URL, else demo
  --languages <l1,l2,…>    one source, several languages (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.12): at least two, the first is the source; translations/<l>/ is written empty, ready for `translate status`
  --spaces <id,…>|none     the audiences (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.1a): use, product, admin, develop (default: the four; asked without --yes), or none: one documentation without spaces; the skeleton keeps their pages and journeys only
  --yes, -y                no question: the detected values and the options as they are

Afterwards, rename the product in doc.config.mjs (product.name) and in content/toc.json (titles).
cli.help.inputs:
Usage: {command} inputs [status] [--json]
       {command} inputs add <code|app|document|workspace|backlog> <value> [options]
       {command} inputs fetch [<name>…]
       {command} inputs ingest [<file>…]
       {command} inputs reconcile [--json]

The sources of the project (inputs.json): what the kit reads besides the code of app.dir. status: each source and its state; add: declares one; fetch: clones or updates the shared repositories into the work folder (inputs/repos/), with your own git credentials (credential manager, SSH key: the kit never sees a token, and a URL with one is refused); ingest: converts the documents (Word .docx, PDF, Markdown, text, HTML, diagrams .drawio .puml .mmd) into text for the documentation agents, in the work folder (inputs/docs/), secrets removed. A Confluence or SharePoint page is read by the skill through the session's connectors (Claude Code, Claude Cowork), never by the kit. reconcile: compares the technologies and the addresses each ingested technical architecture document (DAT) names with the facts of the code ({command} facts), into the work folder (inputs/reconcile.json): found in the code, said by the DAT without a trace, in the code but not in the DAT — a first pass, which the brief architecture-reconcile checks.

Options of add
  code <folder|repository>   --name, --role app|infra|lib, --branch, --depth <n>, --title
  app <url>                  --env (default prod), --read-only
  document <file|url>        --kind dat|spec|guide|other, --title
  workspace <url>            --tool confluence|sharepoint|teams|notion|drive|other (guessed from the address), --title
  backlog <url>              --tool azure|jira|github|gitlab|other (guessed from the address)
cli.help.inventory:
Usage: {command} inventory [--json] | {command} inventory --features [--write] [--force]

Lists what the coverage adapters see in the application (routes, registries, files), family by family: ✔ already cited, · not yet. A page that still holds template guidance does not count.

--features groups them into candidate business features (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.8), by the first static segment of their id: a suggested id (F-01…), routes, API routes, i18n keys, and the sheet that already covers each one, if any.

Options
  --json                   the full inventory (or the candidates with --features) on the standard output
  --features               candidate business features instead of the coverage
  --write                  writes features.json (refused if it already exists, exit code 1)
  --force                  with --write: keeps the existing ids, appends the new candidates
cli.help.new:
Usage: {command} new <page-id> --template <type> [--title "…"] [--parent <id>] [--prefill]

Creates content/<page-id>.md from a page template and declares it in the table of contents; never overwrites. With capture.mode "none", the screen is described by a table instead of a screenshot.

Options
  --template <type>        one of the 31 page types (standard/templates.md): screen, technical, feature, api-surface…; an unknown one lists them all
  --title "…"              title of the page (default: from its id)
  --parent <id>            declares it as a sub-page (level 2) of that page
  --prefill                fills the page's main table from the facts (variables, api-surface, data-model, dependencies, agent-instructions, runbook only)
cli.help.open:
Usage: {command} open [page[~anchor]] [--space <id>]

Opens the built site in the default browser, on a page when one is given.

Options
  --space <id>             the export of that space instead of the full site

DOC_KIT_NO_OPEN=1: only prints the address.
cli.help.optimize:
Usage: {command} optimize [--threshold <KB>] [--quality <0..1>]

Re-encodes the heavy screenshots; the new version is kept only when it is at least 20 % lighter.

Options
  --threshold <KB>         weight above which an image is re-encoded (default 200)
  --quality <0..1>         WebP quality of the re-encoding (default 0.68)
cli.help.pack:
Usage: {command} pack [--output <dir>]

Writes the files the next AI working on the application needs, in the documentation project (never in the application): llms.txt (the outline of the documentation), llms-full.txt (all of it as Markdown), AGENTS.md (the application from the facts: stack, commands, environment variables, data, API, tests, tooling, risks, hotspots) and CLAUDE.md (imports AGENTS.md). A line where a secret detector fires is removed and reported (exit code 1).

Options
  --output <dir>           folder of the files (default: the folder of the built site)
cli.help.skill:
Usage: {command} skill install [--target <skills folder>] [--force] [--hooks [--settings <file>]]

Installs the Claude Code skill of the kit in <skills folder>/{skill} (default: $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills, else ~/.claude/skills); doctor then says whether it is up to date.

Options
  --target <folder>        another skills folder
  --force                  replaces a {skill} folder that this command did not install

--hooks also registers the statistics hook (SubagentStop → scripts/usage-hook.mjs) in .claude/settings.json of the current folder (or --settings <file>): each AI agent's tokens, model and time are then appended to the documentation project's usage/<version>.jsonl. Other settings and hooks are kept.
cli.help.upgrade:
Usage: {command} upgrade [--apply]

Shows the kit changes since the project's kit range, and the migrations to run as a diff (dry run).

Options
  --apply                  writes the migrations and updates the project's kit range
cli.help.view:
Usage: {command} view <page[~anchor]> [--theme light|dark] [--height <px>] [--full] [--tour <n>] [--output <file>] [--space <id>]

Takes a screenshot of a page of the built site (or of a draft build), to review it.

Options
  --theme light|dark       theme of the screenshot (default light)
  --height <px>            height of the window (default 900)
  --full                   the whole page, from its top, in one image (a long page in a single view)
  --tour <n>               shows step n of the page's guided tour
  --output <file>          the PNG file to write
  --space <id>             a page of the export of that space instead of the full site
cli.help.backlog:
Usage: {command} backlog export <azure|jira|github|gitlab|json> [--output <file>] [--all]

Writes the backlog of the documentation — its epics, feature sheets and user stories, with their acceptance criteria — in a tool's import format: azure (Azure DevOps, Boards › Queries › Import work items: a CSV file, the hierarchy by its title columns, the types of backlog.azure.process), jira (Jira Cloud's CSV import: Work item ID, Work type, Parent; the types of backlog.jira.types), gitlab (a project's Issues › Import CSV: title, description), github (GitHub has no import: the issues as JSON, and how to create them with gh and make them sub-issues), json (every item, schemas/backlog.schema.json). Built in memory: an error of the backlog refuses the export (exit code 1, nothing written); what the tool already holds (a reference of that tool: ADO#120, PROJ-7, owner/repo#42) is left out. A line where a secret detector fires is replaced and reported (exit code 1). The kit calls no tool: you import the files.

Options
  --output <file>          the file, its extension replaced (default: beside the built site, <name>-backlog-<target>)
  --all                    also export what the tool already holds
cli.usage:
Usage: {command} [<command>] [options]

Without a command, {command} starts the guided mode: it looks at where you are and suggests the next step.
cli.usage.command.doctor: doctor                   checks the environment and the project, with the fix for each problem (--network)
cli.usage.command.connect: connect                  opens Chromium on the app: sign in, then press Enter to save the session (--url, --forget, --as <role>)
cli.usage.command.demo: demo                     runs the demo data script (capture.setup)
cli.usage.command.capture: capture [patterns…]      takes the screenshots of the capture plans, read-only with a session (--plans, --preview, --no-session, --yes, --compare, --stale, --trace, --verify)
cli.usage.command.record: record <route>           writes a capture plan entry from what you do in the browser (--id, --force)
cli.usage.command.inputs: inputs [add|fetch|ingest|reconcile]   the sources: code repositories, addresses, documents (DAT .docx, PDF), workspaces, backlog (--name, --role, --branch, --depth, --env, --read-only, --kind, --tool, --title)
cli.usage.command.facts: facts                    reads the application code and writes facts/<source>.json (--source, --network, --tools)
cli.usage.command.inventory: inventory                lists what the coverage adapters see (routes, registries…), or the candidate features (--features, --write, --force)
cli.usage.command.bricks: bricks [run] [<id|preset>…]   the state of each brick and why, or runs the bricks named or out of date (--deps, --stale, --force, --network, --tools)
cli.usage.command.probe: probe                    checks a running local or demo instance, GET and HEAD only: headers, cookies, CORS, access control of the routes (--as <role>)
cli.usage.command.dev: dev                      builds, serves and reloads the site while you write (--port)
cli.usage.command.new: new <page-id>            creates a page from a template and adds it to the table of contents (--template, --title, --parent, --prefill)
cli.usage.command.context: context <page…>          the context file of a page for an agent, or its translator's dossier (--budget, --update, --translate <lang>)
cli.usage.command.translate: translate status         the state of the translations; records the pages translated, fixes their anchors (--mark, --all, --fix-anchors, --check)
cli.usage.command.view: view <page[~anchor]>     screenshots a page of the built site (--theme light|dark, --height, --full, --tour N, --output, --space)
cli.usage.command.open: open [page]              opens the built site in the default browser (--space <id>)
cli.usage.command.audit: audit                    measures the maturity level and lists what to do next (report in the work folder)
cli.usage.command.stats: stats                    time, tokens and models per block and per version (--by, --since, --csv)
cli.usage.command.sync: sync                     what the documentation must follow after a change of the application; marks the pages checked (--since, --apply, --labels, --auto-intact, --mark, --all, --sources, --date, --check, --estimate)
cli.usage.command.changes: changes                  what changed in the application since a git reference: routes, tables, variables… (--since, --output, --record)
cli.usage.command.hooks: hooks install            git hooks: facts and sync after each pull and branch switch (uninstall, status, --app <dir>)
cli.usage.command.pack: pack                     files for the next AI: llms.txt, llms-full.txt, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md (--output)
cli.usage.command.backlog: backlog export <target>  the backlog in a tool's import format: azure, jira, github, gitlab, json (--output, --all)
cli.usage.command.export: export <target>          self-contained copy of the project, engine included (--with-dist, --zip)
cli.usage.command.upgrade: upgrade                  shows the changes since the project's kit version and applies migrations (--apply)
cli.usage.command.skill: skill install            installs the Claude Code skill in ~/.claude/skills (--target, --force, --hooks, --settings)
cli.usage.end:
{command} <command> --help (or {command} help <command>) shows the options of a command.
Global options: --project <dir>, --json, --verbose, --lang en|fr, --profile, --help, --version
Exit codes: 0 OK · 1 failed check · 2 usage or configuration · 3 environment
